Warm-up & stretching

🔥 Before weights — 7–10 minutes

The aim is to feel warmer and move more freely, not tire yourself out. These are optional choices, not a circuit you must complete. Avoid painful knee bending.

1. Easy cardio • 5 minutes

Walk on the treadmill at a comfortable pace (roughly 4–5 km/h, flat or gentle incline), or use an easy stationary bike if your knees or back prefer it. You should still be able to talk.

2. Shoulder circles • 30 seconds

Make 10 controlled circles forwards and 10 backwards. Keep shoulders relaxed.

3. Hip hinges • 8 reps

Hands on hips, soften knees slightly, push hips back and return upright. Keep your spine neutral and movement comfortable.

4. Marching or gentle leg swings • 30–60 seconds

Hold a support if needed. Move through a comfortable range; don't force the knees.

5. Practice the first exercise • 1–2 light sets

Use a light weight on your first machine for 8–12 smooth reps; add a second gradually heavier warm-up set if needed. These are separate from your two working sets. Skip any painful movement.

🧘 After weights — optional 4–6 minutes

Cool down with 2–3 minutes of easy walking, then choose a few gentle stretches. Stretching is optional for comfort and flexibility, not a requirement for muscle growth.

Chest doorway stretch • 20–30 seconds each side

Rest forearm lightly on a door frame, step forward until you feel a gentle stretch across the chest. Don't force the shoulder.

Standing calf stretch • 20–30 seconds each side

Hands against a wall, back heel down, lean forwards slightly.

Gentle hamstring stretch • 20–30 seconds each side

Put one heel on a low step, soften the knee, hinge gently at the hips. Avoid rounding your lower back.

Hip flexor stretch • 20–30 seconds each side

Use a short split stance, tuck pelvis slightly and shift weight forwards. Keep the movement small and comfortable.

Upper-back reach • 20–30 seconds

Reach arms forwards at shoulder height and gently spread your shoulder blades without forcing your spine.

🦵 Your knee-friendly rules

Because squatting and getting up from the floor have caused pain around both kneecaps, skip deep squat stretches and any movement that reproduces sharp or increasing pain. Keep the leg press shallow and comfortable. If your knees are worse later or the next day, reduce the load or range next session.

Recurring knee pain affecting everyday movements deserves assessment by a physiotherapist. Stop and seek assessment for swelling, locking, giving way or difficulty bearing weight.

Getting started

Alternate A and B, ideally twice weekly with at least one day between. If a movement causes knee or back pain, stop and adjust. Seek a physiotherapist’s assessment if knee pain persists or worsens. Ask a gym instructor to check machine setup on your first visit.
